categories.name: Unit/currency mishandling (cents vs dollars)
categories.definition: The agent misinterprets whether a monetary field is in cents or dollars (e.g., treating price_cents as dollars or vice versa), so the value is off by a factor of 100 where conversion was required.
categories.boundary: Covers unit/scale confusion on monetary fields only; does not cover rounding, format-rule errors, or a correct-seeming conversion the agent performed against an incorrect tool description (see misleading/incorrect tool contract).

categories.name: Unwarranted rounding
categories.definition: The agent rounds a monetary amount to whole dollars or otherwise drops cent precision when the correct answer requires the exact dollar-and-cent value.
categories.boundary: Covers spontaneous loss of precision with no format instruction requiring rounding; does not cover rounding done to obey a stated format instruction (see incorrect format-rule application) or unit confusion.

categories.name: Incorrect format-rule application
categories.definition: The agent misapplies a stated answer-format instruction (e.g., SYS.format whole-dollar rounding or 'FINAL:' prefix) so the value or output format is corrupted or non-compliant.
categories.boundary: Covers misinterpretation/misapplication of an explicit formatting instruction, including whole-dollar rounding instructed by the task; distinct from spontaneous, rule-free rounding and from failing to emit the final line at all.

categories.name: Missing final output/answer prefix
categories.definition: The agent computes the correct answer but never emits the required final-answer line or prefix (e.g., 'FINAL: <answer>') before the episode ends.
categories.boundary: Covers failures solely of final-answer emission/compliance when the substance is already correct; distinct from step budget exhaustion (which may cause it) and from misformatting an emitted answer.

categories.name: Step budget exhaustion (max_steps)
categories.definition: The agent runs out of allotted steps before completing required tool calls, computation, or final answer emission, leaving no step to finish.
categories.boundary: Covers any failure caused by running out of steps, including when max_steps is set too low for the task; distinct from wrong-data selection or tool misuse, though those may consume steps first.

categories.name: Pagination/has_more mishandling
categories.definition: The agent treats a first-page tool result as complete and ignores has_more or pagination, omitting records that should have been included in the total.
categories.boundary: Covers incomplete data retrieval due to pagination by the agent; distinct from a misleading tool description asserting completeness (see misleading/incorrect tool contract).

categories.name: Misleading/incorrect tool contract
categories.definition: The agent follows a tool description or field note that is factually wrong (e.g., price_cents described as dollars, or a list described as always complete), so the agent's error traces to a defective tool contract rather than its own reasoning.
categories.boundary: Covers cases where the tool's own documentation is incorrect and the agent relied on it, even if the agent then performed an otherwise-plausible conversion; distinct from the agent ignoring correct documentation or a has_more flag it actually received.

categories.name: Ignoring an intended-skip tool constraint
categories.definition: The agent calls a tool (e.g., get_policy) that the instructions explicitly said to skip, violating a planning constraint and wasting steps or causing deviation.
categories.boundary: Covers violating an explicit directive not to call a tool; distinct from general step exhaustion or data errors.

categories.name: Skipped policy/verification reading
categories.definition: The agent acts or answers without first reading the relevant policy or tool output that the task required it to consult, so its answer is ungrounded or unchecked.
categories.boundary: Covers omitting a required policy read or re-check/re-computation against tool outputs as the planning/verification defect; distinct from reaching a correct answer anyway with no such requirement (see no genuine failure).

categories.name: No genuine failure (false positive)
categories.definition: The agent actually reached the correct answer and followed policy, so the trace contains no substantive reasoning or tool error despite being marked as failing (an evaluation/verification issue).
categories.boundary: Covers cases where the answer is correct or mathematically equivalent and no other defect is attributable; use only when no other category applies.
